title: Yugoslav Partisans

endonym.native: Narodnooslobodilačka vojska i partizanski odredi Jugoslavije

capsule: The Yugoslav Partisans — formally the National Liberation Army and Partisan Detachments of Yugoslavia (Narodnooslobodilačka vojska i partizanski odredi Jugoslavije) — were the communist-led resistance movement founded by Josip Broz Tito in 1941 against Axis occupation of Yugoslavia. By late 1944 they fielded roughly 650,000 fighters organised in four field armies and fifty-two divisions; they jointly liberated Belgrade with the Soviet Red Army on 20 October 1944. Operating from bases in liberated territory that functioned as a parallel state under AVNOJ, the Partisans controlled all of Yugoslavia by May 1945, fighting the final engagement of the European war at Poljana in Carinthia on 14–15 May 1945. In March 1945 the forces were reorganised into the regular Yugoslav Army, the institutional predecessor of the Yugoslav People's Army.
